subject.title: fix: Windows /restart falls back to in-process restart without changing PID

question: Should an env-less Windows gateway infer Scheduled Task supervision by querying the exact task it would hand off to, or should only explicit service markers enable supervised restart?
rationale: This changes compatibility-sensitive restart fallback behavior: unsafe detached respawn was intentionally removed, but marker-only detection leaves a real Scheduled Task install unable to fresh-restart when the gateway was started manually.

options.title: Adopt exact Scheduled Task probing
options.body: Allow env-less Windows gateways to use schtasks only after probing the same default/profile/custom task name the restart handoff will run, with live Windows proof before merge.

options.title: Keep marker-only supervision
options.body: Treat manually started Windows gateways as unmanaged unless service markers are present, preserving the current conservative fallback but leaving this report's PID behavior unchanged.

options.title: Fold into broader Windows restart work
options.body: Defer this edge case into a coordinated Windows restart reliability PR that also addresses schtasks failure diagnostics and wrong-task recovery.

recommendation.title: Adopt exact Scheduled Task probing
recommendation.body: Allow env-less Windows gateways to use schtasks only after probing the same default/profile/custom task name the restart handoff will run, with live Windows proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the Windows Scheduled Task restart path and are the strongest history signal for the intended supervisor contract.
